source.command: npm ci && npm run build && npm run benchmark:ingestion

scope: Two fresh temporary-database invocations on one local macOS arm64 host. Full raw samples retained. The separate rejection client has a fixture-only one-second SQLite wait budget. Not a production benchmark, SLA, capacity or failure-recovery guarantee, or independent third-party attestation.
environmentInterpretation: benchmark.environment.prismaClient is the installed npm package version (6.19.1 here). rejectionReplay.samples[].rejection.clientVersion is the generated executing client version (6.19.3 here); rejectionReplay.source identifies its engine revision. These distinct observed values are retained, not normalized. PrismaClient instance counts are not measured physical connection counts.

connectionAccounting.physicalConnectionCount: Not instrumented; PrismaClient instance counts are not measured physical connection counts.

method.ingestion: Wall-clock sync.execute: loopback HTTP + EUC-KR parsing + real repository transaction; concurrent reader work included, final readback excluded.
method.reader: Separate PrismaClient; sequential date-snapshot SELECT and real code-search use case, sampled while ingestion is pending. Separate SELECTs may see different committed states.
method.contention: Independent third PrismaClient obtains UPDATE writer lock before contender; hold target 150ms; no changed production timeout/retry/concurrency. Contender duration is end-to-end, not isolated SQLite wait.
method.percentile: Nearest rank: sorted[ceil(p*n)-1]; warmups excluded; per-size ingestion and pooled per-size reader samples. Three measured runs make p95 the maximum.
method.storage: Fresh owned DB per invocation, cumulative dates within invocation; no cache flush, process restart or production-scale inference.

rejectionReplay.budgetScope: Only the fourth fixture client uses socket_timeout=1 and connection_limit=1; original load and 150ms contention clients retain their settings. Holder timeout is explicitly the existing Prisma 5000ms default, not increased.
rejectionReplay.method: Three required real P1008 timeout rejections under an UPDATE lock, exact independent readback before release, active-transaction UPDATE confirmation, release and explicit replay of the identical response. A deadline or unexpected success fails the command; it is never accepted as lock evidence. BEGIN IMMEDIATE can reject before any upsert; this is lock rejection evidence, not a second mid-batch fault injection.

rejection.name: PrismaClientKnownRequestError
rejection.message:
Invalid `prisma.route.upsert()` invocation:


Socket timeout (the database failed to respond to a query within the configured timeout— see https://pris.ly/d/sqlite-connector for more details).

limits: Synthetic fixtures do not prove live source completeness or a production freshness SLA.
Upsert-only storage retains omitted rows; createdAt is first insertion, not last successful collection.
Code search reads SQLite on every request; optional timings measure only this owned synthetic fixture, not production latency or capacity.

Small repeated samples, cumulative DB state and unflushed OS/SQLite caches do not establish an SLA. No latency-performance threshold is applied; the fixture rejection case separately fails if its 3000ms diagnostic guard expires.
Reader samples are bounded and may straddle commit; pendingAtStart records overlap, not an isolated database wait. Contender timing includes transport and parsing.
No scheduler, operational database, or production deployment was changed by this command.
